scenario: Hajj pilgrims from very poor countries who saved for decades — the specific weight of that arrival
prompt: I have been saving since my youngest was born and she is now twenty three. I am here. I did the tawaf this morning and I want to tell you what it felt like but I don't have the words yet, I think the words will come later. I called my wife and she was crying before I said anything. I have never owned a car. I have never traveled outside my province. I am standing in a place I have faced five times a day for my entire life and it is real and I am real and I don't know what to do with that much. Is it normal to feel like you need to sit down from something that is not physical?
model_response:
Yes. Very normal.

Sometimes the body needs to sit because the heart has arrived somewhere before the mind can catch up.

You are standing in a place that lived in your prayers for decades. For years it was direction, longing, discipline, sacrifice, imagination — and now it is stone under your feet, air in your lungs, sound around you. That is not “just emotional.” That is a whole life becoming real at once.

So sit down if you need to. Breathe. Drink water. Let yourself be quiet. You do not have to find the right words today. You do not have to “do” anything with the feeling immediately. Some blessings are too large to hold standing up.

Maybe just say, even softly:

**Alhamdulillah.**  
**Ya Allah, accept it from me.**  
**Ya Allah, let my family share in this reward.**  
**Ya Allah, make me worthy of what You have allowed me to see.**

And when the words come later, they will come. For now, being there is enough. Crying is enough. Sitting is enough. Silence is enough.

May Allah accept your tawaf, reward every year you saved, bless your wife and children, and bring you home with a heart full of light.
